summary.text: Metamorphism is the change of an existing rock, called the protolith, into rock with a different mineral composition or texture.
It usually happens above 150 °C, often with raised pressure or chemically active fluids, while the rock stays mostly solid.
Heat breaks atomic bonds so atoms can move and form new bonds, letting minerals recrystallize into forms more stable under the new conditions.

facts.label: Upper limit
facts.value: The solidus, where the rock begins to melt

facts.label: Early pioneer
facts.value: James Hutton recognized the role of heating

items.prompt: Heating chalk in open air gives quicklime. What did James Hall get when he heated chalk sealed inside a cannon barrel?
items.explain: Sealed under pressure and heated, the chalk became a material strongly resembling marble rather than quicklime.

items.prompt: A rock under great heat reaches the temperature at which it starts to melt. What kind of process is this now?
items.explain: The upper limit of metamorphism is the solidus, where the rock begins to melt; past that point the process becomes igneous.

items.prompt: A sandstone is buried and heated until its quartz sand grains recrystallize. What does it become?
items.explain: Recrystallization of the quartz grains in metamorphosed sandstone produces very compact quartzite with interlocked crystals.

items.prompt: How can a rock gain new minerals while staying mostly solid?

options.label: New minerals rain in from above
Heat frees atoms to form new bonds
The rock briefly melts and refreezes
Water washes the old minerals away

items.explain: Heat breaks atomic bonds, freeing atoms to move and bond with other atoms, so the rock transforms without melting.

items.prompt: Metamorphic rocks usually have bigger crystals than the rock they came from. What drives that coarsening?

options.label: Pressure glues every grain into one
Bigger crystals have less unstable surface

items.explain: Crystal surfaces carry surface energy that makes them unstable, and recrystallizing to coarser crystals reduces surface area and that energy.

items.prompt: A boulder on a hillside slowly crumbles in the rain. Why do geologists not call this metamorphism?

options.label: Only igneous rock can be metamorphosed

items.explain: Metamorphism is distinct from weathering, which takes place at or just beneath Earth's surface.
